content.key_idea: Checkpointing proceeds in two overlapped, asynchronous phases -- an intra-node GPU-to-CPU snapshot over PCIe, sharded per rank, followed by a CPU-to-Storage persist over the network -- and a timeline shows these phases overlapping with ongoing forward/backward training, stalling only when the snapshot outruns the F&B window.
content.reading_order: Top block: across Node-0 and Node-1's four ranks showing GPU->PCIe->CPU-Memory shards feeding the shared Distributed Persistent Storage; bottom: a left-to-right Train/Checkpoint timeline aligning F&B iterations with Snapshot and Persist phases.

summary: Figure 3 explains the two-phase asynchronous checkpointing workflow that MoC-System builds on. The top half shows four GPU ranks (Rank-0..3) split across two nodes; each rank's Parameters are copied from GPU to a per-rank CPU-Memory shard over PCIe (the GPU-to-CPU snapshot), and all shards are later serialized and written to Distributed Persistent Storage over the network (the CPU-to-Storage persist), illustrating data-parallel sharded checkpointing. The bottom half is a timeline aligning the Train row (forward-and-backward, F&B, iterations with weight updates, U) against the Checkpoint row, showing the Snapshot phase overlapping with F&B of the next iteration and the Persist phase extending further since it does not block training; a red-highlighted stall (S) marks the case where a snapshot overruns its F&B window and blocks training. Together the two halves motivate why shrinking snapshot/persist duration matters.
summary_zh: 图3展示两阶段异步检查点流程：上半部分四个 rank 通过 PCIe 将参数从 GPU 快照到各自 CPU 内存分片，再经网络持久化到分布式存储；下半部分时间线显示快照/持久化阶段与训练 F&B 的重叠，红色标出快照超时导致的训练停顿(S)。
